modelReview.summary: The manuscript is a generic template lacking essential methodological, clinical, and reporting details required for a final-stage review. The analysis is unbound, exploratory, and reports only point estimates without uncertainty or context. The study question is not prespecified, and critical elements (cohort, variables, events, time horizon) are missing. The report does not meet minimal standards for interpretability or reproducibility and cannot support any definitive claims.

findings.title: Unbound exploratory analysis precludes confirmatory interpretation
findings.whyItMatters: The analysis lacks a pre-specified protocol or analysis plan. All findings must be considered exploratory and cannot support causal or clinical conclusions. Any claim beyond description of this specific dataset is unsafe.
findings.actionableFix: Either bind the run to a pre-registered analysis specification or clearly label the entire manuscript as exploratory data analysis with no inferential claims. Remove any language suggesting generalization.

findings.title: Missing cohort description and variable definitions
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript does not describe the study population, inclusion/exclusion criteria, event types, censoring, or the meaning of the treatment variable levels (0 and 1). Without this information, the study context is lost, and results cannot be evaluated.
findings.actionableFix: Add a detailed cohort and variable description, including definitions of survival_time, competing_event, treatment, and the event-of-interest coding. Specify how censoring and competing events were handled.

findings.title: No confidence intervals or uncertainty measures reported
findings.whyItMatters: Cumulative incidence estimates are reported as point estimates only. Readers cannot assess the precision or statistical significance. This severely limits interpretability.
findings.actionableFix: Report 95% confidence intervals for the cumulative incidence estimates at specified time points, or provide the variance-covariance matrix. If the Aalen-Johansen implementation does not provide them, use bootstrap or alternative methods.

findings.title: Ambiguous time horizon for 'final cumulative incidence'
findings.whyItMatters: It is unclear whether the 'final cumulative incidence' refers to the maximum observed time, which can vary between groups and be unstable. Cumulative incidence functions should be reported at clinically meaningful or fixed time points.
findings.actionableFix: Define time points of interest (e.g., 1 year, 5 years) and report cumulative incidence at those points with confidence intervals. Provide the full cumulative incidence curves as a figure (already exists).

findings.title: Statistical method not explicitly justified or described
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript says the method was 'inferred from artifacts' but does not name the specific method (Aalen-Johansen) or justify why it was chosen over other competing risk approaches (e.g., Fine-Gray, cause-specific hazards). This hinders understanding and reproducibility.
findings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the statistical method and provide a brief justification, including why the competing risks framework was needed, and reference the specific estimator and its assumptions (e.g., non-informative censoring).

findings.title: No analytic code provided
findings.whyItMatters: While the run directory contains outputs, there is no code listing showing the exact procedure used to generate the estimates. Reproducibility is limited if the raw data and code are not available.
findings.actionableFix: Include the R or Python script (or equivalent) that produced the Aalen-Johansen estimates, along with any data preprocessing steps, to enable full independent replication.

findings.title: No evaluation of censoring or competing risk assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: The Aalen-Johansen estimator assumes non-informative censoring and correct specification of competing events. There is no assessment of follow-up completeness, loss to follow-up, or other potential informative censoring.
findings.actionableFix: Report summary statistics on follow-up time, number of events (of each type), and number censored. Discuss any potential informative censoring and sensitivity analyses if feasible.

findings.title: Results not connected to any prespecified study question
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript's introduction asks 'What does the analyzed dataset show for the prespecified study question?' but no prespecified question is stated. The analysis appears to be a post-hoc exploration without a clearly defined hypothesis or objective, making it unclear what the findings mean.
findings.actionableFix: State the prespecified study question clearly in the introduction. If no question was prespecified, frame the analysis as exploratory and limit conclusions accordingly.

missingEvidence: Detailed cohort description and participant flow diagram
Variable definitions and event coding (survival_time, competing_event, treatment)
Follow-up time distribution and censoring information
Analytic code (e.g., R/Python script) for reproducibility
Clinical context and rationale for the analysis
